0.0.n: Connects this scene to what came before.

0.2.n: Combines with ご飯 to form 昼ご飯, meaning lunch.

0.3.n: ご飯 means a meal here, not just rice; 昼ご飯 is lunch.

1.0.n: Sets the time frame for their current routine.

1.1.n: Marks 最近 as the time frame being discussed.

1.2.n: Combines with ご飯 to form the word for lunch.

1.3.n: Part of 昼ご飯, referring to the midday meal.

1.4.n: Marks lunch as the topic within the recent time frame.

1.5.n: 制 means a system; 当番制 assigns responsibility by turns.

1.6.n: With する, に marks the arrangement they have chosen.

1.7.n: Polite している from する describes an arrangement they currently maintain.

2.0.n: Introduces the idea of taking responsibility in turns.

2.2.n: Clarifies 当番 by referring to who is responsible for a task.

2.3.n: Shows that 係 is what they decide.

2.4.n: 決める plus ている describes their ongoing practice of deciding responsibilities.

2.5.n: Short for の; adds an explanatory tone before だ.

2.6.n: Plain form of です; joins ん to form the explanatory ending んだ.

2.7.n: Seeks confirmation or signals shared understanding of the arrangement.

3.1.n: Contrasts with 明日 in the next part.

3.2.n: Sets today as the topic, contrasting it with tomorrow.

3.3.n: Refers to the speaker in this example of assigning cooking duties.

3.4.n: Identifies 私 as the person who will cook.

3.5.n: Polite form of 作る; the meal is understood from context.

3.7.n: Sets the time for the husband's turn.

3.8.n: Marks tomorrow as a contrasting topic.

3.9.n: A conversational word for husband; whose husband is understood from context.

3.10.n: Adds a polite or warm tone to 旦那; this is not a name.

3.11.n: Identifies the husband as the person who will cook tomorrow.

3.12.n: Polite form of 作る, referring to a future action because of 明日.

3.14.n: Follows the quoted example to show the sort of arrangement intended.

3.15.n: Turns みたい into みたいに, linking the example to how duties are arranged.

4.0.n: A conversational filler that softens the explanation.

4.1.n: Refers to assigning cooking responsibility in turns.

4.2.n: With する, marks the arrangement they make cooking into.

4.3.n: The connecting て-form of している carries the explanation into the next line.

5.0.n: Points back to the lunchtime already being discussed.

5.1.n: Modifies 時間 through の to specify the lunchtime period.

5.2.n: Links 昼 to 時間, describing which time period is meant.

5.3.n: Refers to the period around lunch.

5.4.n: Marks when the lessons or meetings would take place.

5.5.n: A borrowed word; Japanese does not distinguish singular and plural here.

5.6.n: Marks lessons as what are absent in レッスンがない.

5.7.n: Negative counterpart of ある; says there are no lessons scheduled.

5.8.n: Lists examples of being free, rather than giving an exhaustive list.

5.9.n: A borrowed word referring to scheduled meetings.

5.10.n: Marks meetings as what are absent in ミーティングがない.

5.11.n: Directly modifies 人 as part of the description of someone without scheduled meetings.

5.12.n: The preceding description identifies the person available around lunchtime.

5.13.n: Marks the available person as the one who makes lunch.

5.14.n: Combines with ご飯 to form 昼ご飯, meaning lunch.

5.15.n: Part of 昼ご飯; refers to a meal rather than rice alone.

5.16.n: Marks lunch as what the person makes.

5.17.n: Plain form of 作る states the rule contained in their agreement.

5.19.n: Links the stated rule to 約束, introducing the agreement's content.

5.20.n: Refers to their shared arrangement about who prepares lunch.

5.21.n: Marks 約束 as the object of しています.

5.22.n: Polite している from する; with 約束, describes an agreement currently in place.

0.tip: 昼ご飯 is one word meaning lunch, even though it is split into two tappable parts.

1.lit: Recently, as for lunch, we have made it a rotating duty system.
1.tip: にしています describes a chosen arrangement that remains in effect.

2.tip: んだね signals that the speaker is recognizing or confirming the arrangement.

3.lit: Like, Today I will make it; tomorrow my husband will make it.
3.tip: みたいに introduces an example of how something is done.

4.lit: Well, we have made it a rotating duty, and…
4.tip: していて connects an ongoing arrangement to the explanation that follows.

5.lit: We have an agreement that the person without lessons or meetings at that midday time makes lunch.
5.tip: という links a whole statement to 約束, showing exactly what the agreement says.
